issues.issue: Servicing Advances are 'all customary, reasonable and necessary out of pocket costs and expenses' incurred in servicing, with no list, cap or standard for judging custom, reasonableness or necessity. What a Servicer may advance and recoup off the top of collections is left to argument.

The list of Servicing Agreements includes '(g) the Assignment Agreements,' which are assignment, assumption and recognition agreements rather than servicing agreements. Obligations the Agreement imposes 'under the related Servicing Agreement' therefore have an uncertain referent.

The definition captures 'any Sub-Servicer or Subcontractor,' but the Agreement defines 'Subservicer' and not 'Sub-Servicer.' Whether the participant category matches the defined class of servicing delegates is left unclear.

The closing sentence provides that 'the Stated Principal Balance of a Liquidated Loan is zero,' using a term the Agreement never defines; the defined term is 'Liquidated Mortgage Loan.' The point at which a loan drops out of the balance is fixed by an undefined label.

Subsequent Recoveries are 'unanticipated amounts' received on a liquidated loan, with no test for what was anticipated or by whom. Whether a later recovery counts is a judgment the definition does not constrain.

The definition reads 'any Mortgage Loan that is purchased by the ... originator is an amount equal to the excess,' both ungrammatical and attributing the purchase to the originator, whereas Section 2.03 places substitution and repurchase on the Transferor. Who owes the adjustment amount is garbled.

The Supplemental Interest Trust is held 'for the benefit of the holders of the Senior Certificates and the Mezzanine Certificates,' while Section 2.01(f) has the Cap Contract acknowledged by holders of the Senior Certificates 'other than Group 3 Certificates' and the Mezzanine Certificates. Whether Group 3 holders are beneficiaries of the supplemental trust is not consistently stated.

Trust Administrator Compensation is all investment earnings on the Distribution Account, while Master Servicer Compensation is all investment earnings on the Collection Account and Section 2.01(e) permits the Collection Account to 'be deemed to be a sub-account of the Distribution Account.' If the deeming operates, both definitions claim the same earnings.

The corpus enumerated here omits the Carryover Reserve Fund, the Cap Contract, the Cap Account, the Mezzanine Cap Contract and the Supplemental Interest Trust, which the Preliminary Statement nonetheless treats as assets of the Trust Fund excluded from the REMICs as 'Excluded Trust Assets.' Whether those assets are in the Trust Fund at all cannot be settled from this definition alone.

The NIMS Insurer's rights are made to depend on notes 'issued pursuant to the Indenture,' but 'Indenture' is not a defined term anywhere in this Agreement and no such instrument is identified. Whether and when the NIMS Insurer holds rights cannot be determined from the provision.

The conveyance excludes 'those rights under the Servicing Agreements that do not relate to servicing of the Mortgage Loans,' including Servicer representations and warranties and remedies, 'which rights were retained by the Transferor' — with the parenthetical left unclosed. Which loan-level claims passed to the Trust and which the Transferor kept is precisely what the exclusion leaves open.

Items (B), (C) and (E) are each required only 'except as provided below,' and item (B) allows a mere copy 'certified by the related originator' in place of the original recorded Mortgage. What a complete Mortgage File must contain is therefore qualified in ways the clause does not itself specify.

Item (F) requires UCC assignments 'of the security interest referenced in clause (v) above,' but this list is lettered (A) through (H) and contains no clause (v). The document required cannot be identified from the cross-reference.

The provision states that delivery of the recorded Mortgage and interim assignments shall 'in no event' be later than one year after the Closing Date, then in the proviso allows delivery 'within 720 days following the Closing Date' for the same documents. The two outside dates cannot both control.

The recording carve-out turns on whether recordation is required 'by either Rating Agency,' although the Preliminary Statement designates three Rating Agencies, and the sentence breaks off mid-clause ('may conclusively 47'). Both the scope of the exception and the parties' reliance right are left incomplete.

The clause says only that the parties 'agree and understand that it is not intended' that any listed high-cost loan be included, which states an expectation rather than a representation or covenant, yet it supports an indemnity from the Depositor and the Trust Fund. Whether it creates an enforceable obligation at all is the question it raises.

If an account ceases to be an Eligible Account the responsible party must 'immediately' establish a new one and transfer the funds, with no cure period or notice mechanic and no consequence specified for failure. What 'immediately' requires is undefined.

This clause directs the Trust Administrator to execute, deliver and perform the Cap Contract, whereas the definition of Cap Contract describes it as a contract between the Cap Provider and the Supplemental Interest Trust Trustee. Which capacity of Wells Fargo is the counterparty must be resolved between the two.

The Custodian 'acknowledges receipt of the documents identified in the Initial Certification' rather than of the documents Section 2.01(b) requires to be delivered, so the acknowledgment measures itself by its own certification. What has actually been delivered to the Trust is not established by the acknowledgment.

The Custodian certifies 'based on its review and examination' that the documents 'appear regular on their face,' and in the next sentence is placed 'under no duty or obligation to inspect, review or examine' those same documents. The two statements pull against each other within one provision.

The Custodian must identify the originator for any Mortgage Loan 'with a material exception,' but neither 'material' nor 'exception' is defined or measured against any standard. Which exceptions trigger the disclosure duty is left open.
